review: Independent worldwide catalogue security, data, and release review

checksObservedByReviewer.crawlerSuite: 40 passed, 1 pre-existing Chromium loopback test skipped, 0 failed

checksReportedByImplementerOrParent.disposablePostgresIntegration: passed migrations 001–005, catalogue DB integration, and 3 scheduled-runner checks
checksReportedByImplementerOrParent.childMigration: parent reports migration 005 applied on isolated Neon child with 1186 pre-existing rows preserved
checksReportedByImplementerOrParent.childGrantsImport: backend report records 20 verified Grants.gov rows, unknown locations, incomplete coverage (847 expected; cursor 20) and zero deletions

reviewFindings: Grants.gov robots exception is limited to POST on exact documented API paths; URL allowlist, HTTPS, DNS public-IP pinning, TLS, pacing, response size limit, and redirect denial remain enforced.
SAM.gov API key remains server-side; no keyed redirect is followed; missing key disables SAM without affecting Grants.gov.
Source country and worldwide claims require copied explicit geographic evidence; applicant eligibility does not set location. Expired and forecast notices are not presented as open.

Page limits, cursor units, checkpoint persistence, schema checks, and incomplete coverage prevent partial ingestion from being reported as a complete feed; the importer upserts without deleting absent rows.

Country filtering and search pagination bind to all active filters through a fixed-length cursor fingerprint. Unknown locations remain visible only in Worldwide/all; private saved and paid data retain the existing user transaction and RLS controls.
Migration 005 adds source values, a constrained locations column, conservative Lebanon backfill, and an index; it makes no deletes, billing changes, role grants, or RLS changes.
qualificationLimits: SAM.gov was not live-qualified because no SAM_GOV_API_KEY was configured; it remains opt-in and absent from the default runner.
The daily GitHub source schedule remains inactive; no production migration or deployment is covered by this review.
The independent Chromium loopback test is skipped in the present environment.
Paid matching remains scoped to confirmed Lebanon geography and does not consume new unknown-location records.
A drifting publisher count can leave a partial checkpoint incomplete; documented --refresh starts a new bounded listing pass while existing database records remain preserved.
